posts.body_html:
Ok, so it looks like a grand mix up and since no definitive answer is forth-coming I'll throw in my two cents.
Seems the issue is a bit more complicated because of this . It is supposed to be a true flava ornata from Prince George County and was posted in Terraforums almost a decade ago.


Phil S, earlier in this thread, insists the clone "formerly known as Prince George" isn't (from there). Rather it is a gulf coast plant. Mike calls this plant Gulf Coast now. In Rob Co's post on a Black Vein - Gulf Coast hybrid, Mike commented


 "Phil (F),    Here’s a sibling to Rob’s plant - they can definitely produce amazing colors outdoors: sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/358/flava-ornata-amazing-man-clone    The flava ornata parent plant is the gulf coast, FL clone from Phil Sheridan. With Rob’s particular clone, as you pointed out, there seems to be only a slight “artificial suntan.” Most of that color can be achieved outdoors. "  In older posts (2011) he called this parent Prince George County Va.

I have a division of Mike's (Phil's) gulf coast plant and a division of "Prince George County" from another grower. I can see no more difference than that between two pitchers on the same division. So, I believe they are the same clone. The majority of divisions of this clone out there seem to be identified as Prince George.


Edit:   Actually, I just found the definitive answer here,  sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/713/flava-var-ornata-gulf-coast  in the last post of the thread. So these are the same clone.

The real problem is that location names have become used as clonal names here. A bad idea, this has the potential to create more confusion than already exists. "Is my ornata gulf coast THE ornata Gulf Coast? And what of the other ornata Prince George County clone? Seems it's time this clone got a real clonal name of it's own. (How about it Phil? Mike?)

posts.body_html:
After many years, I finally got around to dividing and transplanting my mother plant, so there's a new update. Here's a blast from the past, a clone that originated from Dr. Phil...Sheridan! As to where this clone originated from, nobody besides Dr. Sheridan knows for sure, but it really does look like an Okaloosa Co, FL genotype to me. that is just speculation of course.

Fortunately, there's no other clone in circulation that has been named S. flava var. ornata gulf coast, FL, and the features are quite unique. Interesting fact: this clone has been extensively bred with and is the parent of all improved black veined plants! Well, excluding Phil's Faulisi's improved version, hehe

Just because it has been extensively bred doesn't mean we have taken these genetics to their fullest potential. Given all the segregation that occurs with the offspring, I'm pretty certain this clone is the result of complex hybridization. Given that fact, if you cross this plant with say this puppy: sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/4503/flava-var-atropurpurea-okaloosa-yellow You'll probably have to run very large numbers before finding the gem we're seeking. Have I made this cross yet? Foolishly, no, just thought it up. I bet somewhere in that combination, a ridiculously veined ornata is just itching to be found. Maybe Leo will get there before I do!

Anyways, the epic S. flava var. ornata Gulf Coast, FL, a clone that has withstood the test of time (well, I've had it since the early 2000's and it's still in high demand!). Pics taken 7/1/19:

posts.body_html:
So, I've posted this pic a few times but have never gotten a response as to if it really is a Gulf Coast ornata or not. It was purchased as such, but looks nothing like your typical GC ornata. Any opinions are welcome. FYI. This plant is a bitch to grow. I've almost lost it twice. It's about as big a pain in the ass as an 'extreme red throat' or rugelii, which tells me it is a deep south clone.

*** Edit! This clone has been identified as flava Bronze. NOT ornata Gulf Coast, FL ***
